# Home inspection report

14 Alder Street, inspected March 2021 for the purchase. Condensed from the inspector's PDF.

## Summary of findings

A 1962 two-story frame house in fair condition overall. Priority items: a cracked rafter over the north bedroom, double-tapped breakers in the panel, an improper water heater relief pipe, and a stair-step crack in the east basement wall. Everything else is routine maintenance.

## Structure and framing

The wall between the kitchen and the dining room is load-bearing: it carries the second-floor joists and sits over the steel beam in the basement. Do not remove it without an engineer. The wall between the hall and the den is a non-bearing partition. The floor framing is 2x10 joists at 16 inches, in good condition.

## Roof and attic

Asphalt shingles with about 8 years of life left. The rafters are 2x6s at 24 inches, and the north slope sags slightly. One rafter over the north bedroom is cracked and should be sistered. Staining on the sheathing suggests past ice dams; add attic insulation and baffles.

## Electrical

A 100-amp panel with a main breaker. Breaker 14 serves two circuits (double-tapped), which is not permitted: an electrician should fix it. No GFCI protection in the garage.

## Plumbing and water heater

Copper supply lines in good condition; the main shut-off is in the basement by the front wall. The gas water heater was installed in 2014, and its relief valve discharge pipe stops 20 inches above the floor, which should run to within 6 inches.

## Foundation and basement

Block foundation. A stair-step crack about 3/16 of an inch wide runs through the mortar joints in the east basement wall, about 4 feet long, with a little efflorescence. The inspector recommends a structural engineer evaluate it and that the crack be monitored. A hairline vertical crack in the northwest corner is cosmetic. No standing water at the time of the inspection.
